rappel_detail.notes: First of four double-rope rappels down the East Face, starting near M&M Ledge.
rappel_detail.anchor: bolted anchor, climber's-left of M&M Ledge
hazards: The M&M Ledge anchor is two pieces of old fixed gear, a pin and a wire. A large and reportedly bomber horn sits up and left of it that would make a much better station and nobody has rigged it - carry cord if you want to use it
Because the line trends left rather than dropping straight down, a rope end blown or thrown off line is awkward to recover
rappel_detail.station: The rappels begin at M&M Ledge. From it, work climber's left to reach good bolts - the bolted stations are not directly beneath where the ledge drops you, and finding them is the only route-finding on this descent. If you rappel from the ledge's own anchor instead, that is a fixed piton and a fixed wire, and the rappel from it also trends climber's left.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the East Face line on double ropes.
hazards: Steep sustained face with nothing to stand on between stations - once on the rope you are committed to reaching the next anchor
rappel_detail.station: Second station on the bolted line down the East Face.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the East Face line on double ropes.
hazards: Anything knocked off a station here falls the full height of the wall
rappel_detail.station: Third station on the bolted line.

rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel, reaching the ground at the base of the East Face.
hazards: Talus and snow at the base of the face for much of the season
rappel_detail.station: Last rappel, essentially reaching the ground at the base of the East Face - the side you approached from, so this is where your pack is.

set.rappels: 4 double-rope rappels from bolted anchors down the East Face, on Thin Red Line’s rappel line from M&M Ledge; or scramble to the summit roped and take the standard Liberty Bell descent.
set.rappel_count_note: Rappelling this route means joining Thin Red Line’s descent at M&M Ledge. Four rappels off bolts, reached by working climber's left from M&M Ledge, and the description that gives that sequence assumes two ropes - four double-rope rappels essentially to the ground. Parties who first rappel from M&M Ledge's own fixed pin-and-wire anchor, which also trends climber's left, count five. No single-rope option is described for this line. The alternative descent, for parties who continue to the true summit rather than rappelling from the ledge, is the standard Liberty Bell notch route - a downclimb east to a two-bolt station and two rappels of about 25 m into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch - which is fewer rappels but lands on the opposite side of the mountain from the East Face approach and from your pack. Per-station distances are not published; the figures given assume near-full-length double-rope rappels.
